newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Court freezes some TNT trade proceeds.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Court freezes some TNT trade proceeds.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Friday that the Federal Court had granted interim freezing orders over the proceeds from some trading in TNT Ltd options.
The orders applied to proceeds from options trading and over open options positions of two clients of Macquarie Equities Ltd and Ord Minnett Ltd, the ASC said.
"The interim freezing orders were granted to enable the ASC to conduct an investigation into certain trading in TNT options prior to the recently announced takeover bid," the ASC said.

The ASC said it had made no allegations of breaches of the Corporations Law by any person. "However, the freezing orders were sought to secure the funds should grounds for action arise as a result of the ASC's inquiries," it said.
The matter will return to court on October 10.

The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) and the ASC said on Thursday they had begun an investigation into options trading in TNT Ltd just before the transport group received a friendly A$2.0 billion takeover bid from Dutch post and telecoms giant Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN).
The ASX, which first took notice of trading in TNT options last week, said it regarded the matter very seriously and had asked the Australian Securities Commission to begin a formal investigation.

Macquarie Equities managing director Warwick Evans said on Thursday that Macquarie was very relaxed about the investigation and believed nothing untoward had happened. Macquarie Equities is a division of Macquarie Bank Ltd.
